passages.text: It is the tears of the earth that keep her smiles in bloom.
passages.note: sorrow and joy bound together; grief that nourishes

passages.text: If you shed tears when you miss the sun, you also miss the stars.
passages.note: dwelling on loss blinds you to what remains

passages.text: Once we dreamt that we were strangers. We wake up to find that we were dear to each other.
Sorrow is hushed into peace in my heart like the evening among the silent trees.
Do not seat your love upon a precipice because it is high.
passages.note: choosing love for status rather than safety

passages.text: What you are you do not see, what you see is your shadow.
I cannot choose the best. The best chooses me.
passages.note: letting go of the need to choose perfectly

passages.text: They throw their shadows before them who carry their lantern on their back.
passages.note: living by the past casts shadows ahead

passages.text: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.
Rest belongs to the work as the eyelids to the eyes.
passages.note: rest as part of good work

passages.text: Man is a born child, his power is the power of growth.
O Beauty, find thyself in love, not in the flattery of thy mirror.
Life finds its wealth by the claims of the world, and its worth by the claims of love.
passages.note: worth found in love, not worldly demands

passages.text: The dry river-bed finds no thanks for its past.
The bird wishes it were a cloud. The cloud wishes it were a bird.
passages.note: envy; wanting to be someone else

passages.text: The waterfall sings, "I find my song, when I find my freedom."
passages.note: freedom as the source of true expression

passages.text: Do not blame your food because you have no appetite.
passages.note: blaming circumstances for your own state

passages.text: You smiled and talked to me of nothing and I felt that for this I had been waiting long.
passages.note: quiet companionship one has longed for

passages.text: He has made his weapons his gods. When his weapons win he is defeated himself.
passages.note: trusting force; winning that defeats you

passages.text: The stars are not afraid to appear like fireflies.
The mind, sharp but not broad, sticks at every point but does not move.
Man does not reveal himself in his history, he struggles up through it.
Like the meeting of the seagulls and the waves we meet and come near. The seagulls fly off, the waves roll away and we depart.
My day is done, and I am like a boat drawn on the beach, listening to the dance-music of the tide in the evening.
passages.note: ageing; the close of a working life

passages.text: Life is given to us, we earn it by giving it.
We come nearest to the great when we are great in humility.
The sparrow is sorry for the peacock at the burden of its tail.
passages.note: burdens of status; pity for the proud

passages.text: Never be afraid of the moments--thus sings the voice of the everlasting.
Take my wine in my own cup, friend. It loses its wreath of foam when poured into that of others.
passages.note: being valued as yourself, not compared

passages.text: Thank the flame for its light, but do not forget the lampholder standing in the shade with constancy of patience.
Tiny grass, your steps are small, but you possess the earth under your tread.
Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can.
"I give my whole water in joy," sings the waterfall, "though little of it is enough for the thirsty."
The woodcutter's axe begged for its handle from the tree. The tree gave it.
passages.note: betrayal; giving to those who harm

passages.text: We read the world wrong and say that it deceives us.
passages.note: blaming the world for our misreading

passages.text: The grass seeks her crowd in the earth. The tree seeks his solitude of the sky.
Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and death like autumn leaves.
He who wants to do good knocks at the gate; he who loves finds the gate open.
The scabbard is content to be dull when it protects the keenness of the sword.
Power said to the world, "You are mine. The world kept it prisoner on her throne. Love said to the world, "I am thine." The world gave it the freedom of her house.
I think of other ages that floated upon the stream of life and love and death and are forgotten, and I feel the freedom of passing away.
passages.note: peace about being forgotten and passing

passages.text: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of life; making it possible to buy with life what is truly precious.
The cloud stood humbly in a corner of the sky. The morning crowned it with splendour.
The dust receives insult and in return offers her flowers.
Do not linger to gather flowers to keep them, but walk on, for flowers will keep themselves blooming all your way.
Do not insult your friend by lending him merits from your own pocket.
I cast my own shadow upon my path, because I have a lamp that has not been lighted.
passages.note: your own unlit potential blocks you

passages.text: Man goes into the noisy crowd to drown his own clamour of silence.
The road is lonely in its crowd for it is not loved.
I carry in my world that flourishes the worlds that have failed.
passages.note: carrying past failures within present success

passages.text: Not hammerstrokes, but dance of the water sings the pebbles into perfection.
Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their thanks when they leave. The gaudy butterfly is sure that the flowers owe thanks to him.
To be outspoken is easy when you do not wait to speak the complete truth.
passages.note: bluntness that is not full honesty

passages.text: If you shut your door to all errors truth will be shut out.
passages.note: fear of mistakes shuts out truth

passages.text: The roots below the earth claim no rewards for making the branches fruitful.
Time is the wealth of change, but the clock in its parody makes it mere change and no wealth.
passages.note: time well used versus merely passing

passages.text: When I travelled to here and to there, I was tired of thee, O Road, but now when thou leadest me to everywhere I am wedded to thee in love.
Let me think that there is one among those stars that guides my life through the dark unknown.
passages.note: hope for guidance through the unknown

passages.text: One sad voice has its nest among the ruins of the years. It sings to me in the night,--"I loved you."
I have my stars in the sky, But oh for my little lamp unlit in my house.
passages.note: neglecting what is close to home

passages.text: The dust of the dead words clings to thee. Wash thy soul with silence.
passages.note: silence to heal after empty words

passages.text: Gaps are left in life through which comes the sad music of death.
The world has opened its heart of light in the morning. Come out, my heart, with thy love to meet it.
passages.note: meeting a new day with love
